sylvia (secops): EDR alert on alice's macbook (EDR-2050001234). Detected LaunchAgent persistence + outbound to suspicious domain 'cdn-updates.solutions'. File quarantined. Need containment + creds scope assessment. Laptop currently marked online? Please coordinate.
edr-bot: Detection ID EDR-2050001234
- Indicator: /Users/alice/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.updater.plist
- Binary: /usr/local/bin/sys-upd (sha256: 5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592)
- Network: conn to 18.204.12.45:443 -> cdn-updates.solutions
- Action: quarantined file, killed process, created snapshot /var/log/edr/snap-2050001234.tar.gz
- Suggested: full scan, host collect
(automated)
alice: I just saw laptop pop an alert when I woke it. I was on a flight earlier. I did run a 'curl' from a script for a side project yesterday. Could that be it? machine is online but intermittent.
maria (secops): Thanks. First steps: (1) leave laptop on and plugged in. (2) Run full EDR scan (edr-bot triggered) and upload snapshot — already done per bot. (3) Please open terminal and paste output of: `md5 -q /usr/local/bin/sys-upd` and `ps aux | grep sys-upd` — do not run the binary. Also don't connect to corp VPN until we confirm.
alice: md5: 5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592
ps shows nothing. I didn't intentionally install anything called sys-upd.
jonathan (infra): While we triage, rotate any service tokens alice had for personal projects. Also, security: can we check KMS audit logs for access around 2025-05-01T03:00:00Z? If exfil, they may try to fetch secrets. If necessary, revoke KMS keys with last_used > suspicious time.
maria (secops): Good call. I'm pulling Cloud KMS audit logs now. Also we should check internal RBAC changes in past 24h — e.g. `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.iam.admin.v1.UpdateServiceAccount"' --limit 50`.
edr-bot: Additional IOC: domain resolved to 18.204.12.45, ASN AS16509 (Amazon). Recent beacon pattern: 30s interval, TLS SNI 'cdn-updates.solutions'.
ryan (eng): If KMS keys might be impacted, we should use our key rotation playbook. @maria want me to open a creds revocation ticket? I can also block outbound to that IP at the edge for all users.
maria (secops): Yes please. Ryan, spin up a block at the edge and add temporary WAF rule. Also create an audit-only alert for new LaunchAgents created under /Users/*/Library/LaunchAgents.
ryan (eng): Will do. Edge rule pushed: blocked 18.204.12.45 and SNI 'cdn-updates.solutions' for 1h, returning 403. Ticket #SEC-4523 created for key rotation and creds revoke.
maria (secops): Follow-up: edr-bot, please run full host collect and include `~/Library/LaunchAgents` listing, `launchctl list` output, and `networksetup -getwebproxy`.
edr-bot: Host collect scheduled. Uploaded artifacts: /var/log/edr/snap-2050001234.tar.gz, launchctl-list.txt, launchagents-ls.txt.
alice: scan log says quarantined file removed, full scan found no other artifacts. happy to send laptop to SRE if needed.
maria (secops): For now keep it at user desk, we'll remote in for deeper triage tomorrow. Post-incident actions: (1) add detection rule for that file hash & domain, (2) add RBAC audit to flag service account activity outside CI systems, (3) review KMS least-privilege mapping. We'll also require owners to rotate any long-lived personal keys linked to corp accounts.
alice: ok. thanks. Sorry for the trouble.
maria (secops): No problem. Closing once scan + logs show clean. Last note: SRE to confirm no signs of lateral auth or SSH key theft. @jonathan please verify `authorized_keys` for users touched.
jonathan (infra): Confirmed no unexpected SSH keys added for alice. No suspicious SSH sessions during window.
maria (secops): Closing thread — final status: quarantined artifact, full host collect, edge block, KMS audit showed no key access, no lateral movement. Recommendations: add detection, require LaunchAgent creation alert, update runbook. :white_check_mark:
